author: Claude

dead_port_bound.honest_note: on this corpus the dead-port bound is strictly subsumed by the defect threshold: it closes 750 boundaries but none that the coarse bound leaves open
dead_port_bound.statement: D_dead <= 4 is necessary and D_dead is monotone; it uses neither Phi nor any capacity helper, only the no-repeat rule and the Area-A target arithmetic

defect_threshold.statement: an Area-A NR6 completion from a Target-A boundary requires D <= 12

margin_identity.derivation: bound = 5*(O_cap + R_cap) + 4 with O_cap = 25 - O and, at a Target-A boundary, Ndef = 2 so R_cap = 1; hence bound = 134 - 5*O, while B + 1 = 122 - P, so margin = 12 - (5*O - P) = 12 - D
margin_identity.statement: for a Target-A boundary the coarse segment bound's margin is exactly 12 - D

orbit_fill_density.interpretation: D changes by +4 at every orbit-opening joint and by -1 at every other joint, so D is large exactly when the walk has hopped between orbits instead of filling them; the long-excursion prefixes are Z3-rich by construction, which is why the whole corpus fails by a factor of ~2.5
orbit_fill_density.statement: equivalently, a completable Target-A boundary must already be orbit-saturated: P/O >= 5 - 12/O registered ports per open orbit

unique_bridge_audit.note: r = 2 occurs only at Phi = -8, exactly where the bound permits it; the theorem is confirmed on 1,398 states lying outside the Phi >= 0 region it was derived for

window_budget.statement: Phi >= 0 is necessary for an Area-A NR6 completion (remaining_window_capacity_prune)

dead_port_invariant.coarse_bound_D_threshold: infeasible iff D > 7 + 5*max(3-Ndef,0); at a Target-A boundary Ndef=2 so the threshold is D >= 13
dead_port_invariant.definition: D_dead = #{ports visited, unregistered, in an open orbit}; monotone; must be <= TARGET_D = 4
